mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p>0.10) in periods where this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 5% signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5% and UNRATE falls by >0.3pp month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average, coupled with a concurrent increase in the housing starts index (HOUST), signals a synchronized expansion in manufacturing and construction, boosting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-mo MA and HOUST > 12-mo MA for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive when both INDPRO and HOUST exceed their 12-month moving averages for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month spike in the federal funds rate to above 5% without a corresponding rise in real GDP growth (GDPC1) signals an aggressive policy tightening that outpaces economic momentum, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5% and GDPC1 growth < 1% YoY in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS > 5% and GDPC1 growth is below 1% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month average, alongside a flat or declining personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1), signals a shift from spending to saving, which reduces near-term demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-mo MA for 3 consecutive months and GDPC1 flat or falling
regime_hint: household deleveraging or precautionary savings episode
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals a deepening labor market weakness, which reduces consumer spending and corporate hiring, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its long-run trend, without a corresponding rise in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL), signals supply-side expansion outpacing inflation, which supports corporate margins and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > long-run trend for 4 consecutive months and CPIAUCSL change < 0.1% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO is above its long-run trend for four months and CPIAUCSL is flat or falling.
